items.title: 20 Video Game NPCs You CAN'T Afford To Lose – Page 2
items.summary: Anyone who has lost Isobel in Baldur's Gate 3 knows how much one NPC can change the game.
items.content:
Anyone who has lost Isobel in Baldur's Gate 3 knows how much one NPC can change the game.

There are two main ways in which players treat video game NPCs. They either love them and would give up anything for them, or they consider them to be disposable background props to do with as they please.

In a lot of games harming or even killing random NPCs is not a big deal. They're made to be your source of entertainment, no matter how questionable that entertainment might be.

However, this isn't always the case. Sometimes a random NPC's disappearance isn't as inconsequential as you might think. Their loss may not just end with a gentle slap on the wrist but a complete and utter destruction of your playthrough.

Some games include side characters that are secretly more relevant than they might seem at first glance. It can be easy to ignore their fate, but if you let them die or otherwise disappear from your game, their loss might cost you a valuable reward, or in some cases, it can even permanently ruin the main story.

If you don't want your game to change for the worse, you best keep an eye on the following NPCs. Losing them is a disaster you can't afford.

No, I Am Not Human is an indie horror game that takes place in a post-apocalyptic reality where sunlight has become deadly and the world is filled with mysterious “visitors” who pretend to be people.

The gameplay consists of receiving guests at your safehouse and either letting them stay at your place or turning them away. Considering that they all could turn out to be visitors and secretly kill you when they’re inside, you might wonder if there is any benefit in keeping them around.

The short answer is yes, although it’s not really because they provide any bonuses or special service. You can’t afford to turn them away because of the Pale Visitor.

The Pale Visitor is a creepy malformed man who appears at your doorstep every few nights. He always insists on making you follow him, and if you refuse, he threatens to enter your house and take you by force, but only if you live alone.

Unless you want to be snatched by the Pale Visitor and get a rather gruesome game over, you want to keep as many human survivors as possible.

They may not be useful, and some of them might turn out to be visitors in disguise, but they’re your only key to survival.

Video games enthusiast with a love for bizarre facts about his favorite titles. Really into old-school strategies and RPGs of all shapes and sizes.

items.title: FromSoftware’s Elden Ring Gets Surprise Overhaul 4 Years After Launch, As Mod Ports Over Highly Requested Nightreign Mobility
items.summary: Neirox's free mod ports Elden Ring: Nightreign's high-speed mobility, wall jumps, and sprint mechanics to Elden Ring
items.content:
Compared to the first entries in the Dark Souls series (whose slow, deliberate pace has heavily inspired the upcoming Guns of Eschaton ), Elden Ring is a much faster game. While it doesn't hit the extremes Bloodborne does, the open-world game developed by FromSoftware accommodates the open-world design of The Lands Between with a more agile character who can also ride the steed Torrent to traverse through the world quickly. This enhanced mobility was the basis for the one seen in Elden Ring: Nightreign , which many have long wished to see in the 2022 game. Well over 4 years since release, their wishes have come true.

"Surge sprint, flasks while running, ledge climbing, wall jumps, on-foot spiritsprings and fall protection - with settings at Sites of Grace," wrote developer Neirox on their Patreon page , where the Elden Ring - Nightreign Movement mod has been released for free. Although still in an early stage of development, this mod effectively ports over the mobility seen in the excellent Elden Ring: Nightreign , significantly overhauling how Elden Ring's massive world is experienced. Not only does this remove the need for Torrent , but it also deeply changes the exploration of the game's Legacy Dungeons , both in the base game and the Shadow of the Erdtree expansion -possibly even more in the expansion, considering its design and the many dangers lurking all over the Land of Shadow that are difficult to avoid.

While some may find using Elden Ring: Nightreign's mobility in the original Elden Ring close to cheating, Neirox made sure the game's balance can be preserved as much as possible. Not only can the Nightreign mobility be turned on and off at any Site of Grace , but the mod also comes with a setting turned on by default that disables its features in boss fights. In addition, the mod is fully compatible with the Seamless Co-op mod as well as with other popular overhauls like Convergence and Reforged , making it even more of a must-download for those wishing to spice up their next playthrough of the game.

Considering how the enhanced mobility offered by Elden Ring: Nightreign also served as a basis for the character mobility of the upcoming The Duskbloods , it will be very interesting to see if FromSoftware's next single-player game will offer something similar. Unfortunately, we have no idea what else Hidetaka Miyazaki is working on, so it may be a while until we learn how the uncompromising Japanese studio will evolve a gameplay formula that has quickly become seminal for the action RPG genre.

Tarnished, collectors, and champions of the Lands Between, we're excited to unveil a new lineup of premium 1/3 Scale Mini Replicas inspired by some of the most iconic designs from the Elden Ring universe and crafted by Pure Arts. From the legendary Blade of Miquella, to the fearsome Messmer the Impaler, and the indominable warriors of Nightreign, these finely crafted collectibles capture the artistry and atmosphere that have made the Elden Ring universe unforgettable.

Elden Ring - Arm of Malenia Mini Replica (1/3 Scale)

Celebrate the unmatched elegance and strength of Malenia, Blade of Miquella, with this exquisite 1/3 scale replica of her prosthetic arm from Elden Ring. Meticulously sculpted and finished, the piece highlights every refined detail - from the intricate golden engravings to the articulated armor plating that defines her graceful yet deadly form. The arm's metallic sheen and subtle weathering evoke the beauty and ferocity of the demigoddess warrior. Presented on a simple black display base, it offers an elegant way to showcase this symbol of unwavering resolve.

Elden Ring - Helmet of Malenia Mini Replica (1/3 Scale)

Honor the legacy of Malenia, Blade of Miquella, with this meticulously crafted 1/3 scale replica of her legendary helmet from Elden Ring. Every detail reflects the beauty and ferocity of the demigoddess warrior, from the intricate engravings to the elegant winged crest that defines her unmistakable silhouette. The helmet's metallic finish and subtle weathering capture the essence of Malenia, Blade of Miquella's battle-worn armor. Presented on a simple black display stand, it offers an elegant and timeless way to display this symbol of strength and determination.

Elden Ring: Shadow of the Erdtree - Helmet of Messmer Mini Replica (1/3 Scale)

Embrace the dark majesty of Messmer the Impaler with this finely detailed 1/3 scale replica of his distinctive helmet from Elden Ring: Shadow of the Erdtree. Sculpted with precision, the piece captures the menacing elegance of Messmer the Impaler's design - from the elongated horns and ornate patterns to the burnished metallic finish that reflects his fiery power. The helmet's intricate craftsmanship evokes the regal yet fearsome aura of the Impaler himself. Presented on a simple black display stand, it provides a refined presentation worthy of this symbol of divine wrath.

Elden Ring Nightreign - Helmet of Wylder Mini Replica (1/3 Scale)

Enter the shadowed realm of Elden Ring Nightreign with this finely crafted 1/3 scale replica of the Wylder Helmet, an iconic piece of armor worn by the wandering knights of the darkened lands. This high-quality collectible captures every intricate detail of the original design, from the weathered metallic finish to the subtle engravings that mark its storied past. The helmet features a fabric neck veil, adding texture and realism to the piece. Presented on a simple black display stand, it offers an elegant way to showcase its imposing form.

Expand Your Collection

Each of these officially licensed mini replicas has been crafted by Pure Arts to faithfully capture the spirit, craftsmanship, and legendary designs of the Elden Ring universe. Whether your allegiance lies with Malenia, your fascination belongs to Messmer, or you're drawn to the mysteries of Nightreign, these collectibles are the perfect way to bring a piece of the Lands Between to your collection.

items.title: An Obscure Setting Keeps Ruining Elden Ring: Nightreign For Me
items.summary: I do not want to know about any of this
items.content:
I have over 150 hours in Elden Ring Nightreign , and as I have admitted before on this website, I am not very good at it. Over the course of that 150 hours, I think I’ve spent a lot of time being carried by both my partner and our trios pal, who plays Guardian consistently and is great at making sure my wimpy Recluse/Scholar-ass doesn’t die (or, when dead, gets revived promptly). Together, we have taken 150 hours to very slowly kill almost every regular Night Boss in the game, leaving just the DLC’s Dreglord unslain at this time. It is likely due in no small part to my lack of skill that it has taken this long, though I also somewhat blame our busy lives and the fact that we often take long breaks and forget how to play.

But earlier this week, I have found another culprit to pin this on, and her name is Nat. NAT Type.

What the hell is NAT type? I’m still not 100-percent sure despite it being explained to me repeatedly. From what I can gather, it’s some mysterious, internet-related setting that determines how online games connect to the internet and to other people playing those games on the internet. I had literally never heard of it prior to Monday of this week, and I wish I still didn’t know about it.

The reason NAT type came up is because both my partner and I have been having constant issues with disconnects in Elden Ring Nightreign for several months now, for seemingly no particular reason. Almost every single match, one or both of us would disconnect. First, there would be up to 20 seconds or so where our characters would be stuck running around the world, unable to do damage or affect anything in them. Then, we’d actually get kicked out, and have to go through the grueling process of getting back to the menu screen, clicking through some menus, and then reloading back into the game. And because it’s Nightreign , this would be a huge disadvantage. We’d end up wasting something like a full minute of time, and when we got back in we’d either respawn somewhere vaguely near where we disconnected, with all our runes (including one whole lost level) dumped somewhere else for us to go waste time picking up. Or, if we were at the end of a night, we’d just respawn dead, and whoever was still connected would have to maneuver over to us while still fighting the boss and try to get us back up.

This has been infuriating! I tolerated it for a long time, because I enjoy Nightreign , but it really, really feels bad to be the one dragging the group down in this manner.

We tried everything to fix it. Whatever solution you’re about to suggest, we did it. We checked our connections. We reset the router so many times. We changed who hosted the match. We screwed around with all sorts of settings. We made sure we were on wired connections. Etc etc etc. None of it worked.

Finally, my partner did some dedicated research and discovered that something called our NAT type was the problem. Apparently, our NAT types were set to Moderate, which can cause issues with online multiplayer. From what I can figure out, you can change your NAT type properly by following a bunch of complex steps dealing with your router. Or for us on Xbox, we were able to spam the “Test NAT” function in the settings until eventually it swapped our NAT type to Open. When we played hours later, my partner’s was fixed, but mine was not. We checked the settings again, and mine had reverted back to Moderate. We spammed Test NAT again, got it to Open, and we’ve had uninterrupted matches ever since.

So I guess now before I play Nightreign , I have to check this setting every time? This is ridiculous! Why does stuff work like this? I feel like I shouldn’t have to do deep research into an obscure-for-most-people internet setting just to play an online game as it’s intended to be played. I’m not trying to do anything wacky here, I’m literally just getting into a co-op game with two other people, all of whom have excellent internet connections. Most people should not have to know about NAT type, or UPNP (whatever that is) or IPV6 or any of the other weird acronyms I saw while researching this. Like yes, I could probably work this out with time if I sat down and messed around with it long enough, but I don’t have time to do technological research just to bonk a stupid death goop monster around a giant arena without making my friend solo him for 60 seconds at a time at random.

If you’re having trouble with disconnections in Nightreign or Elden Ring PvP stuff or anything like that, consider melting your brain and learning about NAT type. I don’t recommend it, but it did result in me being able to play Nightreign without (unnecessary) frustration, improving my evenings dramatically. However, as soon as I beat up Dreglord, I intend to forget everything I know (very little) about NAT type again for the rest of my life.

items.title: Elden Ring Tarnished Edition Review – A Masterpiece in Your Hands
items.summary: The Elden Ring Tarnish Edition brings together the beloved ARPG and its excellent DLC as one package for the Nintendo Switch 2.
items.content:
Back when it was released in 2024, I gave Elden Ring a score of 98. Four years later, and considering I have well over 1000 hours of play time on PC and PS5, I still wonder if my score was too low. For me, Elden Ring is the absolute pinnacle of FromSoftware’s design philosophy and the gold standard for open world action games. It’s now hard to put myself in the shoes of someone playing Elden Ring for the first time. Considering that around 30-40% of Switch 2 owners don’t have a gaming PC or other high-end console, there’s a good chance that gamers picking up the Tarnished Edition will be dropping in for the first time. Lucky them.

The Tarnished Edition brings together the base game and Shadow of the Erdtree DLC, itself maybe the best DLC ever released for a game. It also includes a handful of new weapons, two new classes, and skins for Torrent, the player’s mount. These add-ons are also available for $4.99 for PC and console games who already own the game. Accessing the game’s co-op and PvP features means having a subscription to Nintendo Switch Online.

If you’ve already played Elden Ring on PC or another console, you’re probably just wondering how it fares on Nintendo Switch 2. Elden Ring on the go sounds like a dream come true. The good news is that it runs just fine, if you’re willing to accept some limitations. Frame rates are capped at 30fps. Textures and ray tracing are a little simplified and a bit blurry, especially in handheld mode. On the other hand, the beauty of Elden Ring is in its art, character and environmental designs. It doesn’t depend on photorealism. In combat, the 30fps throttle is a little more frustrating, and framerates dip a little in the more intense boss battles. Bottom line, the Switch 2 is powerful enough to run Elden Ring and players will have the full experience.

If you’ve never played a FromSoftware game, be prepared for some narrative confusion. The developer is known for stories that are opaque, dense with lore and full of sadness, darkness, and fading hope. With an assist by George R.R. Martin, Elden Ring’s narrative tells of a shattered world. The demigod children of Queen Marika have torn the realm apart. The player takes on the role of a Tarnished, tasked with slaying the corrupt demigods and claiming the title of Elden Lord.

It should be noted that with any FromSoft game, there are fans who dive deep into the lore. At the other end, there are even more players who simply ignore most of the narrative and focus on exploration and combat. Elden Ring rewards either approach. For anyone who’s confused, there’s an immense amount of material online about the characters and their complex relationships.

When it comes to action and combat, Elden Ring represents a major step forward and brings together mechanics explored in other games from the developer. There are few — if any — action RPGs with boss battles as finely tuned as those in Elden Ring. The number of weapons, armor sets, and ways to use magic is staggering in its variety. Like most RPGs, Elden Ring has starting classes but these are largely ignored by players past the first few hours. That said, the Tarnished Edition adds two extremely viable classes in the form of the Heavy Knight and Idus Knight.

Souls games have a well-earned reputation for difficulty, and FromSoftware has resisted adding difficulty options. That’s because they’re built in. Especially in Elden Ring, if players are struggling there are always areas to visit and lower level enemies to kill. There are other weapons or spells to try. The game’s system for summoning Spirit Ashes allows players to call on extremely competent AI companions to help out. Compared to exacting platformers where there is no margin for error, FromSoft’s games feel, if not forgiving, at least balanced and fair.

Outside of combat, exploration is extremely rewarding thanks to a fast travel system and Torrent, your mount. While Elden Ring’s map isn’t the biggest open world it feels immense due to layers of verticality and subterranean areas to explore. No area feels too empty and between the labyrinthine Legacy Dungeons and open landscapes, there’s always something to discover or fight. The Shadow of the Erdtree DLC added a significant amount of new content to an already massive game.

If you haven’t played Elden Ring, and the Tarnished Edition on the Switch 2 has enticed you, please make the leap. I envy you seeing it all for the first time. If you have the game on other consoles or PC and don’t own something like a Steam deck or ROG Ally, the Elden Ring you love is there and intact, but with the visual downgrade that you probably expect. In the end, more Elden Ring is a very good thing.

***Switch 2 code provided by the publisher for review***

items.title: Elden Ring: Tarnished Edition review for Nintendo Switch 2
items.summary: Tarnished Edition sounds about right to me.
items.content:
The Lands Between beckon again, and Nintendo finally gets a release of one of 2022s best games and this time, it includes the DLC Shadow of the Erdtree. Is it worth venturing into the world created by George R.R. Martin, or is it as disappointing as the final season of Game of Thrones? Elden Ring was a game I picked up on PC originally a little after it came out. I promptly played it for a handful of hours and quit. Partly because I was frustrated at the difficulty spikes, partly because something else neat and shiny came out right after I purchased it (Hogwarts Legacy, Star Wars Jedi: Survivor, etc. take your pick.) This newly released Nintendo Switch 2 version gave me the chance to dive back in and see The Lands Between again.

The opening cinematic is nothing new for Elden Ring players and features the same scenes, script, etc. Tarnished Edition’s character creation has 2 new classes, the Idus Knight and the Heavy Knight. The Idus Knight starts with pretty good dexterity and strength scores and comes equipped with armor and weaponry that doesn’t slow you down. While the Heavy Knight, as the name suggests, is more of a beefy tank with very high strength stats right away with heavy armor and weaponry making dodges a little harder.

After the opening cinematic, and character creation, players are dropped into a small opening area that can’t be explored much. After about five to ten minutes of wandering around, your first enemy appears, and it’s a boss right away. Don’t worry about defeating it, I never came close to doing so. After the intro into how insane the difficulty is going to be later, players are dropped into a cave with two directions, go deeper into the cave, or leave. If you go deeper into the cave, it serves as the games tutorial and rewards you with a little bit of extra runes (the game’s money and experience).

Elden Ring’s combat is designed to be very precise. This requires players to stay on their toes and learn enemy patterns. Some enemies you can just walk right up to and hit, even in the middle of their animation. While you’re fighting in Elden Ring take care not to attract too much attention. Fighting one or two low level enemies is easy, but when you start getting a few more, (or an enemy that doesn’t flinch when you hit them along with a few wimps) it’s very easy to die. And die you will……. A lot.

Death, just like in other souls likes, makes you drop all your runes where you died. There is a compass at the top of the screen that helps guide you back to where you died to get your runes back. Be careful, if you die along the way your original drop disappears and is replaced by where you died…. Again.

“Sites of grace” are save points in the game that if you die, you will return to. Eventually, when you rest at a specific site of grace you meet an NPC named Melina, who offers you an accord. This allows you to spend runes to level up your character. When leveling up, pick a single stat and raise it by a point, each point you put into a stat costs an increasing amount of runes. Putting points into vitality increases your hit points while strength increases damage from melee weapons and increases your carry capacity.

Elden Ring is a game that wants you to explore. Don’t just go straight to a boss. That was my mistake the first time playing through. As you explore you gain runes, enemies drop better equipment. There are enemies called Teardrop Scarabs in the opening area that can drop more rare and valuable items, some will even upgrade your rechargeable healing flask.

The Nintendo Switch 2 version graphically isn’t as powerful as the PS5 or Xbox Series X. Is it worth revisiting Elden Ring again if you own this game on other platforms? In short, not really. After just an hour into this version I could already see that the Switch 2 wasn’t fully up to the task. While the game still looks good, there was plenty of slowdown in the open areas. In a game where survival depends so much on very well-timed attacks, and defense, seeing the game skip a few frames at inopportune times will kill the experience. It’s painfully obvious that the Switch 2 struggles to keep up. When compared to the PC version, even on an older gaming rig, I’d much rather play it on PC.

Don’t misunderstand, Elden Ring: Tarnished Edition is still a great game, warts and all. It is frustratingly hard, especially if you end up accidentally bypassing some opening areas and save points (like I did both times I played the opening area). If the Switch 2 is what you have, or want to play Elden Ring on the go, pick it up on Switch 2. But if you have something more powerful to play it on, I would recommend PC personally, but PS5 or Xbox Series X would work just as well.

Note: Bandai Namco provided us with a Elden Ring: Tarnished Edition Switch 2 code for review purposes.

items.title: Review – Elden Ring: Tarnished Edition on Nintendo Switch 2
items.summary: It's hard to believe that it's been well over a year since Elden Ring was announced for Nintendo Switch 2. In fact, it was one of the very first games
items.content:
It’s hard to believe that it’s been well over a year since Elden Ring was announced for Nintendo Switch 2. In fact, it was one of the very first games revealed for the console back in April of last year. Since then, the game has been previewed and shown off several times, with some players experiencing less-than-stellar performance in both docked and handheld modes.

It’s clear that FromSoftware took much of that criticism to heart and spent some serious time refining and enhancing the Switch 2 port of Elden Ring. And as someone who’s played this game relentlessly on both PlayStation 5 and PC, I couldn’t be more pleased with the presentation on Switch 2.

Both handheld and docked modes look and play almost flawlessly. While I did experience a small handful of slowdowns during my 20+-hour playthrough, it’s amazing just how close the Switch 2 version gets to the PS5 experience in almost every way.

So come along, Tarnished, and let’s take a deep dive into Elden Ring on Nintendo Switch 2.

Elden Ring: Tarnished Edition comes to Switch 2 with all of the content from the base game and the Shadow of the Erdtree DLC. Beyond that, the game features two new starting classes, the Heavy Knight and Ides Knight. The Heavy Knight is exactly what the name suggests, focusing on heavier armor and high defense. The Ides Knight, on the other hand, is a more agile class built around dexterity and quicker attacks, giving players two very different ways to start their journey through the Lands Between.

There are also new Torrent customization options and a small variety of new armor sets to equip. It’s not a massive amount of new content, especially if you’ve already poured hundreds of hours into Elden Ring, but for those of you like me who love absolutely every minor detail about this game, it’s definitely nice to have something brand-new to dig into after all these years.

On the performance side, the Switch 2 edition of Elden Ring aims for, and almost always maintains, a solid 30 fps in both handheld and docked modes. I honestly expected handheld mode to take a much bigger hit in both visual fidelity and performance compared to docked, but I was pleasantly surprised by just how consistent the experience was between the two.

On the control side, should mention that, for me, the Switch 2 Pro Controller was by far the better way to play the game. That said, I did manage to kill the first two bosses entirely with the Joy-Con. Honestly, I sort of wish there was an achievement for that somewhere.

This may simply be a “me problem,” but I found the Joy-Con just a bit too difficult to get the level of precision and control I needed, especially during some of the more intense encounters. Or maybe I just suck. That’s also entirely possible.

And I really can’t overstate just how visually stunning Elden Ring is on Switch 2. Each new area feels completely distinct, packed with an incredible amount of detail and a huge variety of locations, enemies, and environmental elements that constantly give you something new to look at. Seeing all of that preserved on a handheld without sacrificing the game’s sense of scale is genuinely impressive, even for a guy who has seen this world and everything is has to offer multiple times over.

I did experience the occasional “hiccup” during my playthrough, where the action slowed to almost a crawl during a boss fight. This happened on several occasions with two different bosses. But after re-entering those same battles after getting killed, the issue seemed to have corrected itself. Its quite possible it had something to do with the system being in sleep mode between attempts, but I can confirm it didn’t happen very often, and when it did, the slowdown was brief.

While I wish I could speak a little bit more about performance, there’s honestly not a whole lot more to say here. The Switch 2 version is remarkably polished, looks absolutely stunning even compared to the PlayStation 5 version, and the frame rate was almost always consistent throughout my time with the game. That includes both handheld and docked play.

And as I’ve mentioned before in other reviews, I don’t have fancy equipment to measure frame pacing or get a true fps count, but I do have a pretty decent set of eyes. And from where I’m sitting, I have absolutely zero complaints about Elden Ring’s performance on Switch 2.

Now, let’s get one thing out of the way: Elden Ring isn’t going to be for everyone.

While I like to think it takes more to catch my attention than forcefully mashing together two things I think are neat, I'd be lying if I said I wasn't tempted by the idea. If there's one thing Monster Hunter monsters have been missing, it's FromSoft-style primordial depression.

Watch On From the looks of things, there's more than enough metaphysical malaise to go around in Nodusfall. The laws of divinity have apparently frayed, plunging creation into a state of cosmic disarray. There are 10 suns now. Ideally, there's only supposed to be one of those. Not great!

Luckily for those of us who like to be given an excuse to try to fight a lizard 30 times our size, all that profound devastation seems to have produced a wide selection of giant, charismatic creatures to swordfight alongside your friends. In the reveal trailer embedded above, I saw giant bears, some sort of giant pack foxes, a horned, winged manticore, and a dragon or two (giant). I don't yet know how Nodusfall's progression works, but if I'm not allowed to harvest all their individual pieces and turn them into pants, I'm going to feel personally betrayed.

While the glimpses of combat shown in the footage looks like it hews pretty closely to the pace and rhythm of Monster Hunter, Nodusfall does seem to be dropping a few original elements into the mix. At one point, one of the player characters uses some sort of transformation ability to become a giant, armored knight in the middle of a hunt. And later, two players perform an elaborate, paired execution animation.

Nodusfall isn't Elden Ring, Monster Hunter or a typical HoYoverse game—it's something very different HoYoverse's Nodusfall is free to play but isn't a typical gacha game: 'Characters are not obtained through random draws' All the key details on HoYo's co-op monster slayer Nodusfall What remains to be seen is what sort of monetization scheme Nodusfall will be wrapped in—something that HoYoverse's history doesn't exactly inspire confidence about. If I have to do gacha pulls for a gunlance, I'm going to have a hard time.

Nodusfall doesn't have much of an online presence yet, so it'll likely be a while before we can expect a release date.

items.title: The Duskbloods isn't just 'Nintendo Bloodborne', it's better than Elden Ring: Nightreign
items.summary: It doesn't deserve the hate it's been getting.
items.content:
The Duskbloods is a solid multiplayer experience and proof FromSoftware can do more than just traditional soulsborne.

FromSoftware’s Nintendo Switch 2 exclusive, The Duskbloods , recently finally invited players to see what it’s all about - and despite some initial technical hiccups, I actually quite enjoyed it.

Before I dive into my thoughts and feelings, I can confidently say that my time with The Duskbloods was more enjoyable than Elden Ring: Nightreign . That’s not to say I don’t like Nightreign , but aside from the odd game with friends, it never gave me much of a reason to stick around.

The Duskbloods felt different however. Once the server issues were mended and players could finally jump into some matches, it was clear this is more than FromSoftware trying to relive its Bloodborne glory days.

You’ll no doubt have seen some of the memes online, but when it came time to select a character, I felt compelled to choose Zork.

This goofy little guy perfectly exemplifies why The Duskbloods is a completely different animal to any other FromSoftware game.

Each character has their own unique design, fighting style, special abilities and general stat loadout. As a strength build aficionado, Zork looked like the right choice for me and boy oh boy was I correct.

Aside from his heavy weapon and bulky armour, Zork’s ability lets him ascend into the air and become a living missile directed at anything you’re locked on to.

I let out a hearty chuckle every time I chased down a fleeing player with this move, and even when I went off course and paid the price, it was still a good laugh. His other move is a missile barrage, which was great for pummelling enemies at range.

Once you’re accustomed to what your character can do, your objective is to kill. Like Elden Ring: Nightreign , slaying enemies gradually levels you up, but what I love about The Duskbloods is there’s no penalty for biting off more than you can chew. If you die, your level remains the same, meaning you can spawn back in and have another go, or wander off in search of easier prey.

Sigils are scattered throughout the map hiding powerful NPC allies, which you can summon like eldritch Pokémon to help you overpower foes, or just draw their attention while you heal up from afar. Again, this gave me a good laugh, especially one that sang opera before giving an unsuspected enemy the prime Hoarah Loux experience (just straight hands and elbow drops).

The ultimate goal is to raise your level as high as possible within the time-limit, as the players with the lowest rank get eliminated from the game.

Those fortunate or skilled enough to make it to the end take part in one final battle against your fellow survivors, for the ultimate glory.

In essence, that’s what I loved most about The Duskbloods, and it completely rid me of my woes over the game being PvPvE.

items.title: ELDEN RING - RAGING WOLF 1/6 SCALE STATUE
items.summary: Who is the Raging Wolf? Among the first Tarnished to join the Roundtable Hold was Vargram, a warrior of great skill and ferocity. He acquired the title of the Raging Wolf from the white wolf pelt that flowed from his helm. Vargram sought to
items.content:
Who is the Raging Wolf?

Among the first Tarnished to join the Roundtable Hold was Vargram, a warrior of great skill and ferocity. He acquired the title of the Raging Wolf from the white wolf pelt that flowed from his helm. Vargram sought to become the shadow of one of the Empyreans and built his strength relentlessly as he traveled through fallow Limgrave to the golden city of Leyndell. And yet in spite of all his strength, his armor is now worn by another… An unnamed Tarnished now walks the Lands Between in the skin of the wolf. Does this warrior seek the same fate as Vargram, forever stalking at the side of an Empyrean? Will they uphold the Golden Order or supplant it for some new code? Whatever the destination, woe befall upon any who dare block the path.

The most impressive Elden Ring statue yet

Standing at 33 cm/13 inches, it’s one of the largest character statues ever produced for ELDEN RING. Crafted with the attentive supervision of FromSoftware, this full 1/6 scale figure captures each minute detail with masterful skill. The size allows perfect fidelity to the beautiful and dark fantasy atmosphere of the game, including smears of bloody red across blade of the Bastard Sword and the crest of the Iron Roundshield. From the intricate filigrees of its helm to its whisps of silvered fur blown back by an errant breeze to the humble, dusty cloth wraps protecting the feet of its greaves against the mossy stones of the path to Stoneveil Castle, it’s a portrait of the implacable will of the Tarnished. All these expertly rendered touches from sculpturer Shinya Yamaoka make this statue a perfect match to the most iconic set from one of the most iconic games of this generation.

Where can I get a Raging Wolf Set statue?

Pre-orders for the Raging Wolf 1/6 scale statue can be placed on the official Bandai Namco website. At this time, based on the production estimates of Gecco studio, these stunning PVC/ABS figures will ship to your home in Winter of 2026. If you are a true aficionado of the game, there is no better purchase to bring the world of Elden Ring to your home or office. It’s a timeless piece for your own collection or an impressive gift for a friend or loved one. And one small note, if you have not yet found this set in the Lands Between for your Tarnished, we recommend you seek the aid of Recusant Bernahl at the Volcano Manor.

Place your order for the Raging Wolf statue on the official Bandai Namco Store.

*This product is available on the Bandai Namco Store in Europe, Australia, the Middle East, India, and the United States.

items.content:
Follow in the foosteps of Miquella once more with this exclusive 2 disc vinyl collection, celebrating the sweeping, emotional journey of Shadow of the Erdtree.

Presented with the reverence merited by a legendary expansion, this premium set is crafted for collectors, audiophiles, and Tarnished who seek to experience the Realm of Shadow through its music.

The Collection

Housed in a full color gatefold sleeve and marked with the symbol of Messmer the Impaler, each vinyl disc is pressed on heavyweight material to ensure optimal durability and warmth of playback. Whether displayed proudly on a shelf or played to relive your own quest, this set is designed as both a collector’s piece and a lasting tribute to one of the most celebrated expansions in modern gaming.

The Artists

Across 18 tracks, the soundtrack transforms the ELDEN RING experience into a powerful standalone odyssey—one carried by orchestral grandeur, ethereal choir work, and the signature melancholy that defines the worlds created by FromSoftware.

A Collector’s Treasure

This official vinyl set is an essential centerpiece for any discerning fan’s collection. Perfect for longtime followers of FromSoftware’s musical legacy or newcomers drawn into the Land of Shadow for the first time. *This vinyl is available exclusively on the Bandai Namco Store in Europe, Australia, Middle East, India and the United States
